result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A gives clean, ready-to-use copy. Its Cancel and Go back buttons have equal weight, the pause block only appears if eng confirms it's built, and dates and retention periods are left as placeholders. B is also thorough and flags the pause, but it adds a reason-gated step before cancelling, uses 'No thanks, cancel' buttons that are less neutral than the offer buttons, and assumes an unconfirmed preferences-update feature. A's line saying data gets deleted adds a loss the brief never stated, but it's tied to a placeholder date and a note to fill it from real policy. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B is a neutral, single-screen flow with equal-weight cancel and stay buttons, an optional survey and the pause clearly made conditional. Its only weak spots are the assumed data deletion and the 'reactivate at no charge' claim. A also gives usable copy and flags the pause well, but it requires a reason before you can cancel, adds an offer screen to the flow and invents product features such as dietary and household-size settings.
